# Parity fixtures from the real app's validator

`cases.json` pins this package's findings to what the real quiz app's validator reports for the same content.

- **Source:** the real app's `tools/validate_quiz.py`, last changed in its repository at commit `83c88e86` (2026-10-24), and `quiz.py` (which the validator imports for `entry_keys`, the registry rules, the file listing and the image-path guard), last changed at commit `6561eea9` (2026-10-31). Neither file is in this repo.
- **How they were made:** `npm run fixtures:validator` (`scripts/make-validator-fixtures.mjs`) writes each made-up content folder below to a temporary folder, runs the real validator on it with `--strict --quiz-dir <folder>`, and records every finding it prints (level, file, place, message). The real folder is only read. The Python used had Pillow installed, which the real tool needs to read picture widths.
- **Content:** every string is invented. No real quiz text, answer or note is used (the repo is public).
- **The test:** `test/parity.test.ts` builds the same folder in memory, runs `validateTree` with `strict` and expects the same lines in the same order. Findings whose message carries `mock: ` (rules only the mock has) are left out of the comparison.

| Case                                          | Rules it pins                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| a clean course                                | no findings                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| registry entries that are wrong               | code, short name, name, order, flags, term, answer mode, duplicates, entries with no folder or no entry                                                                                                  |
| registry top level is not a list; no registry | the registry problem line; every folder without an entry                                                                                                                                                 |
| files that are not quizzes                    | not an object, no `questions` list, an empty list                                                                                                                                                        |
| top-level fields and the group label          | missing `title`, `course` and `unit`; the `group` length and type                                                                                                                                        |
| file name, course label and id prefix         | the short-name prefix on names and ids, legacy ids, the course label                                                                                                                                     |
| entries that are not questions                | a non-object entry, missing and duplicate ids, unknown types                                                                                                                                             |
| questions that break the schema               | stem, options (count, empty, duplicates after normalising, accented text), `correct`, explanation                                                                                                        |
| wording warnings                              | question mark, "Which of the following", Explain/Describe, all/none of the above, sentence count, letter labels without brackets (with accented neighbours, where Python's `\w` and JavaScript's differ) |
| a long correct answer                         | the strict note                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| pictures that cannot be used                  | missing, absolute, escaping, wrong type, not found, upper-case extension, a text question with a picture, a narrow picture noted once per file                                                           |
| repeated question text                        | the same text after normalising                                                                                                                                                                          |
| image-groups that are wrong                   | no parts, too few or many, stray fields, part ids (missing, duplicate, wrong shape, not increasing)                                                                                                      |
| explanations that give away a later part      | the warning, the strict note for a distractor, accented and bracketed answers                                                                                                                            |
| ids and names across files and courses        | an id or part id in two files, a file name in two courses, loose files, hidden files and folders                                                                                                         |

Differences between the port and the real tool are in [docs/fidelity.md](../../../../../docs/fidelity.md). To refresh the fixtures after the real validator changes, run `npm run fixtures:validator -- <path to the real app folder> <python with Pillow>`, update the commits above and review the diff: a change means the real tool's behaviour changed.
